title: 33-Facet Atlas Vocabulary — Legacy Level Framework
purpose: Preserve the useful topical breadth of the earlier 33-level information architecture without competing with the current D1-D11 spiritual/transformational Axis. The numbered items below are now facet identifiers/categories, not metaphysical or navigational dimensions.

supersession.rule: D1-D11 is the active vertical spiritual/project-symbolic navigation scaffold: D4 ordinary world map, D5 North Door, D6-D11 ascent, D3-D1 descent.
supersession.legacy_use: The former 33 levels survive as cross-cutting filters/facets that can be applied within any suitable map, network, timeline, provenance or Axis view.
supersession.warning: Never show 33 as a competing count of spiritual dimensions or staircase levels.

bands.name: Orientation
bands.meaning: Direction, source, axis and the conditions for knowing where a record sits.

bands.name: Matter
bands.meaning: Physical substrate, objects, land, energy and built environments.

bands.name: Life
bands.meaning: Biology, ecology, bodies, growth, health and reproduction.

bands.name: Mind
bands.meaning: Perception, memory, knowledge, language, information and interpretation.

bands.name: People & Relations
bands.meaning: Persons, families, communities, peoples, migration and social relationships.

bands.name: Institutions
bands.meaning: Organizations, government, firms, schools, religions and durable coordination systems.

bands.name: Law & Civilization
bands.meaning: Law, property, rights, constitutions, culture, norms and historical civilization.

bands.name: Systems & History
bands.meaning: Economy, finance, energy, infrastructure, technology, trade, war and historical change.

bands.name: Meaning & Spirit
bands.meaning: Values, worldview, religion, symbolism, purpose and the project's interpretive layer.

facets.name: Meaning
facets.description: Questions of purpose, value and what a record means within a larger frame.

facets.name: Spirit & Worldview
facets.description: Religious, philosophical and spiritual systems that orient human interpretation.

facets.name: Systems
facets.description: Interacting economic, technological, infrastructural and political systems.

facets.name: History
facets.description: Events, sequences, inherited conditions, turning points and consequences.

facets.name: Strategic Relationships
facets.description: Dependencies, alliances, bottlenecks, obligations and major cross-system links.

facets.name: Civilization
facets.description: Large-scale patterns of institutions, culture, technology and collective organization.

facets.name: Law
facets.description: Formal rules, rights, duties, enforcement and legal institutions.

facets.name: Property & Control
facets.description: Ownership, control, land, assets, intellectual property and effective power.

facets.name: Constitution
facets.description: The distribution and limitation of political authority.

facets.name: Institutions
facets.description: Organizations that persist through time and coordinate people and resources.

facets.name: Government
facets.description: Public authorities, administration, budgets, regulation and state capacity.

facets.name: Economy Institutions
facets.description: Firms, banks, markets, funds and organizations coordinating production and capital.

facets.name: Social Institutions
facets.description: Schools, religious bodies, families, associations and cultural organizations.

facets.name: Relations
facets.description: Kinship, friendship, cooperation, conflict, exchange and other social ties.

facets.name: Communities
facets.description: People organized by place, language, belief, occupation, culture or shared identity.

facets.name: Peoples
facets.description: Ethnolinguistic, indigenous, national, diasporic and historical populations.

facets.name: Persons
facets.description: Individuals as actors with identities, biographies, roles and relationships.

facets.name: Mind
facets.description: Cognition, attention, perception, memory and interpretation.

facets.name: Knowledge
facets.description: Evidence, learning, science, expertise, archives and information systems.

facets.name: Language
facets.description: Systems through which people encode, transmit and negotiate meaning.

facets.name: Perception
facets.description: How observers encounter, classify and experience the world.

facets.name: Health & Reproduction
facets.description: Health, care, reproduction, development and biological continuity.

facets.name: Ecology
facets.description: Relationships among organisms, environments, resources and ecological processes.

facets.name: Bodies
facets.description: Human and non-human bodies as biological and social realities.

facets.name: Growth & Life
facets.description: Birth, growth, renewal, adaptation and processes that sustain living systems.

facets.name: Built Environment
facets.description: Buildings, settlements and engineered environments.

facets.name: Infrastructure Matter
facets.description: Physical networks such as roads, rail, ports, grids, pipes and cables.

facets.name: Energy & Resources
facets.description: Energy, minerals, water, land and other material foundations of society.

facets.name: Objects & Land
facets.description: Physical things, territories and material assets that anchor records in space.

facets.name: Plane
facets.description: Horizontal field in which records coexist and relationships can be observed.

facets.name: Axis
facets.description: Structural orientation/change-of-description principle across views.

facets.name: Ladder
facets.description: Traversable sequence connecting different representations or states without erasing differences.

facets.name: North / Source
facets.description: Project orientation/reference and source-facing meaning; not a replacement for D11 North of North.

examples: D3 + History = provenance chronology and turning points
D4 + Infrastructure Matter = real ports, grids, cables, roads and facilities
D4 + Strategic Relationships = alliances, dependencies, funding and supply-chain links
D8 + Institutions = federated/compositional organizations and shared systems
D9 + Language = translation, messaging and information-relay networks
D10 + Systems = integrated system overview and intervention analysis
epistemic_rule: Facets organize content. They do not alter the evidence class or reality status of the records they filter.
